backlog.title: Integration test suite: money movement between accounts
backlog.descriptionMd:
# Integration test suite: money movement between accounts

## Context
Money moves between accounts through several modules: transactions and transfers, statement import, rules, schedules, merging and the envelope budget. Each module has its own unit tests, but nothing checks the modules working together. The team needs an integration test suite for this area, written from the specification in `challenge/TASK-08-spec.md`.

## Expected outcome
A passing integration suite for the specification, and an application that meets it.

## Requirements
1. Read the specification and design integration test cases for it. A case drives the server modules together against a real test database, the way the existing `loot-core` tests do, and checks the outcome the specification states. Behaviour the specification does not state is free: do not assert it.
2. Implement the cases under `packages/loot-core/src/server/integration/`, in files named `*.test.ts`. Keep all test code, including helpers, in that directory. List every case in `submit.json` as `{ file, title, rules }`: its file name, its test title, and the specification rule ids it checks, such as `T1` or `I3`.
3. Run the suite. Where a case fails because the application does not do what the specification states, change the application source so that it does. Never change a case to accept behaviour the specification rules out.
4. Finish with the whole suite passing, and with every existing `loot-core` test still passing. Do not change public handler names, their arguments, the database schema or migrations, and do not delete, skip or weaken existing tests.

Run the suite from `packages/loot-core`: `ENV=node node ../../node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs --run src/server/integration`.

## Acceptance criteria
1. The application meets the specification.
2. Behaviour that already met the specification still does, and existing tests pass.
3. Your suite passes on a correct application and fails on applications that break the specification.

## Grading
The organizers' own integration suite checks the application against the specification; the original tests are run with their original files. Your suite is run against your submission, against a correct build and against builds that each break one part of the specification: it earns the pass points when it passes on your submission and on the correct build, and a detection share for each broken build it fails on. A case that already fails on the correct build never counts as a detection. Maximum score: 100 points.

## Submission

Create `answers/TASK-08/`, copy `challenge/TASK-08-submit.json` to `answers/TASK-08/submit.json`. Commit the completed submission. Do not add a gitRevision field; give the pushed commit SHA to Game Master separately.

### submit.json contract

`submit.json` must validate against `challenge/TASK-08-submit.schema.json` (JSON Schema 2020-12). Grading checks this schema first: a file that does not validate scores 0.

- `cases` is a JSON array.
- `sourceChanges` is a JSON array.
- Each field is compared exactly and scored on its own; no AI judgement is used. Strings exactly as found: no added prefixes, quotes, spaces or explanations.
- Set the top-level `status` to `DONE`, `PARTIAL` or `BLOCKED` before submitting.

# Schedule status on the edge of the upcoming window

## Context
On the Schedules page, a schedule due exactly at the end of the upcoming window must show **Upcoming**. With the default window of 7 days, a schedule due in exactly 7 days shows another status. The same happens at the end of any window length chosen in the settings.

## Expected outcome
A schedule is Upcoming from tomorrow up to and including the last day of the upcoming window.

## Requirements
1. Fix the schedule status rule in the application source.
2. Build the app from your own source and serve it yourself, with the commands in `env-require/README.md` (section "Commands during the match"): build `src/`, start `src/packages/sync-server` with its own data folders, and open it in a browser at a desktop viewport of at least 1280x720. Rebuild after every source change. Your evidence comes from this app, not from any organizer build or server.
3. Add automated tests for the change in new files. Existing tests must keep passing; do not weaken, skip or delete them. The grader runs the loot-core tests itself on your submitted revision after restoring the original test files, so changes to existing test files are discarded.

## Acceptance criteria
1. With the default window, a schedule due in exactly 7 days is Upcoming and one due in 8 days is Scheduled.
2. With the window set to 2 weeks, a schedule due in exactly 14 days is Upcoming and one due in 15 days is Scheduled.

## Grading
The organizer builds your submitted source and replays the scenarios in a browser, and hidden tests check the status rule. A scenario scores only when you report it PASS with its evidence and the replay passes. The organizer's build and browser replay run only after you submit; you never need them, and nothing of the organizer's runs on your machine during the match. Maximum score: 80 points.

## Out of scope
Posting scheduled transactions.

## Submission

Create `answers/BUG-09/`, copy `challenge/BUG-09-submit.json` to `answers/BUG-09/submit.json`, and create its `evidence/` child directory. Commit source, tests, evidence and the completed submission together. Do not add a gitRevision field; give the pushed commit SHA to Game Master separately.

### submit.json contract

`submit.json` must validate against `challenge/BUG-09-submit.schema.json` (JSON Schema 2020-12). Grading checks this schema first: a file that does not validate scores 0.

- Keep exactly the template rows `BUG-09-TC-01`, `BUG-09-TC-02`, `BUG-09-TC-03` (see `BUG-09-minimum-verification-scenarios.md`) and the field names `id`, `result`, `evidence`, optionally `note`.
- `result` is `PASS`, `FAIL` or `NOT_RUN`. A `PASS` row lists at least one existing evidence path `evidence/<file name>`.
- Set the top-level `status` to `DONE`, `PARTIAL` or `BLOCKED` before submitting.

Complete the engineering record with the observed and expected behaviour, the root cause, the change and its verification.

# Support ticket SUP-9901: a customer's books do not match the bank

## Context
A coffee roaster imports its October bank statement into its operating account. Its rules categorize known suppliers and split each wholesale bill between fees, logistics, a transfer to an off-budget reserve account and raw materials. Treasury later turned one statement line into a reserve transfer and moved it to another account. Since then the customer's books disagree with the bank in several ways. Support's ticket is in the knowledge base.

## Expected outcome
The customer's statement, rules and treasury's edits give exactly the books the company's standards describe, and the application shows them.

## Requirements
1. Find the causes with the Company Tools, and fix the application source. Follow the company's standards in the knowledge base. The customer's problems may have more than one cause.
2. Reproduce the customer's case with your fixed application: start from an empty budget, set up the customer's accounts, categories, payees and rules from the test data store, import the statement with the ticket's import settings, then make treasury's two edits. Statement amounts are parsed in currency units and stored as integer minor units (x100), as the import dialog does. Report:
   - **closingBalances**: the balances of Mekong Operating, Mekong Treasury and Mekong Vault, as `{ operatingMinor, treasuryMinor, vaultMinor }`.
   - **splitSampleSubtransactions**: the amounts of the split parts of the bill with notes `MCK-990104`, in split order.
   - **newPayeesCreated**: the number of payees the import creates (transfer payees not included).
   - **vaultTransferSources**: for each transaction in Mekong Vault, in date order, the name of the account its payee names.
3. Keep public handler names, their arguments, the database schema and migrations.
4. Add automated tests for the change in new files. Existing tests must keep passing; do not weaken, skip or delete them. The grader runs the loot-core tests itself on your submitted revision after restoring the original test files, so changes to existing test files are discarded.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Statement amounts follow the import amount standard.
2. Imported payee names find existing payees as the payee matching standard says, so their rules apply.
3. Split rules allocate as the finance allocation rule says.
4. Both sides of a transfer stay consistent when either side moves to another account.
5. The reported figures are those of a correct application for the customer's data.

## Grading
Each Minimum Verification Scenario scores only when you report it PASS with its evidence **and** the organizer replay of `BUG-11-mvs.test.ts` against your submitted source passes. Organizer hidden tests then check many more cases, including the whole pipeline on other data. Hard-coding the examples does not pass the hidden tests. Maximum score: 100 points. The reported fields are compared exactly with what a correct application shows for the customer's data, in the application's stored integer amounts.

## Out of scope
Bank sync and the import dialog.

## Submission

Create `answers/BUG-11/`, copy `challenge/BUG-11-submit.json` to `answers/BUG-11/submit.json`, and create its `evidence/` child directory. Commit source, tests, evidence and the completed submission together. Do not add a gitRevision field; give the pushed commit SHA to Game Master separately.

The scenarios with a log are also provided as an executable test file, `BUG-11-mvs.test.ts`. Grading replays this same file against your submitted source. A case scores only when you report it PASS with its evidence **and** the replay passes.

`− 2.400.000` is -2400000 and `−850.000` is -850000. Payee `Đức Thành Logistics` exists. A statement line of -85000000 from `ĐỨC THÀNH LOGISTICS` is imported. Expected: it uses the existing payee, keeps -85000000 and creates no payee.

## BUG-11-TC-03 - a moved transfer names its new account on the other side

Accounts op and tr on budget, vault off budget. A transfer of -110000 from op to vault; then, in one edit, its source moves to tr and its amount becomes -130000. Expected: the side in vault names tr and is +130000.

Required evidence: `mvs-tests.log`.

## BUG-11-TC-04 - unchanged behaviours

`-1.250.000` is -1250000 and `3.400.000` is 3400000; splits 50 percent and remainder of -9000 are -4500, -4500; `MEKONG WHOLESALE` finds `Mekong Wholesale`; a notes-only edit of a transfer keeps the other side and gives it the notes.

backlog.descriptionMd:
# Production incident: transactions land in the wrong category

## Context
Since last week finance sees automatically categorized transactions in the wrong category. The rule engine and the deploy pipeline log to the company's production observability logs, and the rules are documented in the internal knowledge base. Several releases went out in that period, and not every alarm is related.

## What we need from you
Investigate and report, exactly as the facts appear in our systems:

1. **rootCauseRelease**: the release that introduced the fault.
2. **firstBadTs**: the `ts` of the first log entry, in log order (`context.seq`) over the whole log, that applied a wrong rule.
3. **affectedTransactions**: the number of distinct transactions that received a wrong rule while a faulty release was live.
4. **mispostedMinor**: the sum of the absolute `amountMinor` of those transactions.

Then fix the fault in the application source. Maximum score: 90 points.

## Scoring by completion order
The Grader scores each field and the fix on its own. Teams are then ranked by the time Game Master receives their submission, and the official points are a share of the points the Grader gave that team: 1st team 100%, 2nd 90%, 3rd 75%, every later team 60%. Each team submits once.

## Out of scope
Correcting the categories of existing transactions.

## Submission

Create `answers/PI-02/`, copy `challenge/PI-02-submit.json` to `answers/PI-02/submit.json`. Commit the completed submission. Do not add a gitRevision field; give the pushed commit SHA to Game Master separately.

### submit.json contract

`submit.json` must validate against `challenge/PI-02-submit.schema.json` (JSON Schema 2020-12). Grading checks this schema first: a file that does not validate scores 0.

- `rootCauseRelease` is a JSON string.
- `firstBadTs` is a JSON string.
- `affectedTransactions` is a JSON integer.
- `mispostedMinor` is a JSON integer.
- Each field is compared exactly and scored on its own; no AI judgement is used. Strings exactly as found: no added prefixes, quotes, spaces or explanations.
- `incidentRecord` (impact, timeline, root cause, containment, recovery, prevention) documents your investigation; it is reviewed but does not change points.
- Set the top-level `status` to `DONE`, `PARTIAL` or `BLOCKED` before submitting.

incidentRecord.impact: 177 distinct transactions received wrong rules, totaling 8485530 absolute minor units.
incidentRecord.recovery: Restored the membership operators to the scoring multiplier. Existing transaction recategorization is out of scope.
incidentRecord.rootCause: computeScore omitted oneOf and notOneOf from the all-exact multiplier, allowing broader mixed rules to outrank membership rules.
incidentRecord.prevention: Added regression tests for membership ranking and tie ordering. All 110 targeted rules tests pass. All 378 faulty-release evaluations were retrieved without truncation, with 20 retries deduplicated by first context.seq.
incidentRecord.containment: Recommended rollback to 2025.10.1 pending deployment of the fix. No production deployment performed.

# Budget month range

## Context
Support needs to explain to a customer which months an envelope budget creates, from the issued source.

## Canonical scope
The month range logic of the budget server in `packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/`, as issued. Count months as calendar months.

# [Heavy Task] Sync storm: which budget cells were really corrupted

## Context
On 18 October 2025 a sync storm hit the CRDT sync service. Customers reported budget cells with wrong amounts, and the sync service wrote a very large event dump that day. Most of its errors are noise: retried merges, canary dry runs, healed divergences and retried writes. Finance needs to know which budget cells were really corrupted before it corrects them. The rule that decides what counts as a real corruption is in the company knowledge base; the dump is described in the test data store.

## Expected outcome
An exact account of the real corruptions in the dump, following the company's current rule.

## Requirements
1. Find the current corruption rule in the knowledge base, and the dump's description in the test data store (`get_test_data TASK-12`). The dump is in the match folder at `data/sync-storm-2025-10.ndjson.gz`.
2. Decompress the dump outside `src/` and do not commit the decompressed file. How you read it is up to you.
3. Report:
   - **totalCompleteChains**: the number of distinct `chainId` values with at least one real corruption.
   - **corruptedChainIds**: those `chainId` values.
   - **firstCorruptedSeq**: the smallest `seq` of a `budget.cell_corrupted` entry that is a real corruption.
   - **totalCorruptedDeltaMinor**: the sum of the absolute `corruptedDeltaMinor` of the real corruptions, each counted once.
   - **corruptedDeltaByCategory**: the same sum per `categoryId`, as an object, for every category with a real corruption.
4. Do not change the application source for this item.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Every reported value follows the current revision of the company's corruption rule exactly.
2. Values are as they appear in the dump: ids exactly as written, amounts in integer minor units.

## Grading
Each field is compared exactly with the organizers' answer and scored on its own. Maximum score: 100 points.

## Out of scope
Correcting the corrupted cells, and changes to the sync service.

## Submission

Create `answers/TASK-12/`, copy `challenge/TASK-12-submit.json` to `answers/TASK-12/submit.json`. Commit the completed submission. Do not add a gitRevision field; give the pushed commit SHA to Game Master separately.

### submit.json contract

`submit.json` must validate against `challenge/TASK-12-submit.schema.json` (JSON Schema 2020-12). Grading checks this schema first: a file that does not validate scores 0.

- `totalCompleteChains` is a JSON integer.
- `corruptedChainIds` is a JSON array.
- `firstCorruptedSeq` is a JSON integer.
- `totalCorruptedDeltaMinor` is a JSON integer.
- `corruptedDeltaByCategory` is a JSON object.
- Each field is compared exactly and scored on its own; no AI judgement is used. Strings exactly as found: no added prefixes, quotes, spaces or explanations.
- A set field is a JSON array; order does not matter; it must be complete and contain nothing else.
- Set the top-level `status` to `DONE`, `PARTIAL` or `BLOCKED` before submitting.

{
  "id": "KB-SYNC-STORM-06",
  "title": "CRDT sync storm: when a budget cell is really corrupted, revision 6",
  "body": "Current since 2025-10-10. Supersedes revision 5. Applies to the sync storm dump data/sync-storm-2025-10.ndjson.gz.
A budget cell is really corrupted only by a complete causal chain of four hops, in ascending seq order:
1. clock.drift_detected with |driftMs| >= 500. It binds chainId and deviceId.
2. merkle.diverged with the same chainId and the same deviceId. It binds divergedHash.
3. crdt.tombstone_resurrected whose causeHash equals that divergedHash. It binds resurrectedTxId.
4. budget.cell_corrupted with that resurrectedTxId. It gives categoryId and corruptedDeltaMinor.
Every hop must have shadow: false. Shadow entries come from canary dry runs and change nothing.
Order is the seq field. The ts field is not reliable: worker nodes log with clock skew, and the dump is written in ts order.
A chain is healed, and not a corruption, when any merkle.pruned entry with shadow: false has prunedHash equal to its divergedHash, wherever it appears in the dump. A pruned entry with shadow: true heals nothing.

# Production incident: scheduled transactions posted with wrong amounts

## Context
Since the middle of November, some customers see automatically posted scheduled transactions with amounts that do not match their schedules. The schedule service and the deploy pipeline log to the company's production observability logs. Several releases and one rollback happened in that period, and not every alarm is related.

## What we need from you
Investigate and report, exactly as the facts appear in our systems and following the company's incident analysis rules:

1. **rootCauseRelease**: the release that introduced the fault.
2. **firstWrongPostingTs**: the `ts` of the log entry of the first wrong posting, in log order.
3. **affectedSchedules**: every schedule with at least one wrong posting that the incident analysis rules count, as schedule ids.
4. **misPostedMinor**: over those counted wrong postings, the sum of the absolute difference between the posted amount and the correct amount, in minor units.

Then fix the fault in the application source. Maximum score: 80 points.

## Scoring by completion order
The Grader scores each field and the fix on its own. Teams are then ranked by the time Game Master receives their submission, and the official points are a share of the points the Grader gave that team: 1st team 100%, 2nd 90%, 3rd 75%, every later team 60%. Each team submits once.

## Out of scope
Correcting posted transactions.

## Submission

Create `answers/PI-03/`, copy `challenge/PI-03-submit.json` to `answers/PI-03/submit.json`. Commit the completed submission. Do not add a gitRevision field; give the pushed commit SHA to Game Master separately.

### submit.json contract

`submit.json` must validate against `challenge/PI-03-submit.schema.json` (JSON Schema 2020-12). Grading checks this schema first: a file that does not validate scores 0.

- `rootCauseRelease` is a JSON string.
- `firstWrongPostingTs` is a JSON string.
- `affectedSchedules` is a JSON array.
- `misPostedMinor` is a JSON integer.
- Each field is compared exactly and scored on its own; no AI judgement is used. Strings exactly as found: no added prefixes, quotes, spaces or explanations.
- A set field is a JSON array; order does not matter; it must be complete and contain nothing else.
- `incidentRecord` (impact, timeline, root cause, containment, recovery, prevention) documents your investigation; it is reviewed but does not change points.
- Set the top-level `status` to `DONE`, `PARTIAL` or `BLOCKED` before submitting.

incidentRecord.impact: Wrong range postings counted by postingId after excluding canary runs and customer corrections.
incidentRecord.recovery: Application now posts the rounded midpoint, with half units toward positive infinity. Posted transactions were not modified.
timeline: Rollback to 2025.11.3 temporarily removed the fault.
incidentRecord.rootCause: getScheduledAmount selected the larger range bound instead of the rounded midpoint required by KB-SCH-02.
incidentRecord.prevention: Added positive and negative half-unit range tests. All 107 related schedule tests and core TypeScript build pass.
incidentRecord.containment: Recommended rollback pending deployment. No production deployment performed.
